WA-2025-SB6246.title: Concerning emissions from emissions-intensive, trade-exposed facilities under the climate commitment act.
WA-2025-SB6246.summary:
North American Industry Classification System Codes. The NAICS codes applying to EITEs in the Program are those classifications in existence as of January 1, 2026.

Recommendations to the Legislature. By December 1, 2026, Ecology must provide recommendations to the Legislature regarding the schedule of allowances to be provided to EITEs between 2035-2050. The recommendations must identify:
• a proposed method for making annual reductions to EITE allowance allocation that would ensure the total no-cost allowances allocated align with the annual allowance budgets and which are consistent with the state GHG emission limits, including the percentage reductions in EITE allowance allocation that would be applied each year between 2035-2050;
• proposed criteria and methods for Ecology to make adjustments to no-cost allowances allocated to EITEs to address significant changes in leakage risk and to achieve the purposes of the Program;
• the proposed design of an allowance allocation policy or method that would require a portion of no-cost allowances to be consigned to auction and for the proceeds to be invested in projects or programs to reduce GHG emissions at EITEs, including the percentage of allowances to be consigned and methods for the distribution and use of consigned funds;
• additional state policies or strategies that may be necessary to support decarbonization of EITEs to achieve the state GHG emission limits; and
• provisions of the CCA or other state laws needing to be amended to implement the recommendations above.

Ecology must consider input received from representatives of EITEs, other covered entities, environmental advocates, overburdened communities, tribes, other experts, and the public.

If the Legislature does not adopt a schedule of allowances to be provided to EITEs between 2035-2050 by December 1, 2027, they must continue receiving no-cost allowances as provided in the third compliance period until a schedule is adopted.

Emissions-Intensive, Trade-Exposed Facilities Reporting and Planning Requirements. Legislative intent language provides that these requirements are intended as a reporting and planning framework to: achieve emission reductions at EITEs consistent with the total allowance budget and state GHG emission limits; provide financial incentives for early actions taken by EITEs; and consider these actions when Ecology determines grant recipients of CCA funds.

An owner or operator of an EITE must provide the following to Ecology:
• by March 31, 2028, and every two years thereafter, information about the GHG emissions of each EITE facility and, to the extent as determined feasible by Ecology, each unit within each facility, including:
• the products, and volumes of such products, produced by the facility;
• a qualitative description of the sources of emissions from the facility; and

WA-2025-SB5520.title: Concerning the wrongly convicted persons act.
WA-2025-SB5520.summary:
Who May Bring a Claim .

The definition of "actually innocent" is revised and means a person for whom a preponderance of all the evidence no longer supports a finding that the person engaged in conduct that is the basis for a felony charged in the charging document.

The definition of "significant new exculpatory information" is added to mean any information, without regard to its admissibility in court, that:
• supports or is consistent with a person's claim that the person was wrongly convicted; and
• was not considered by the finder of fact at trial or in a plea hearing before conviction.

A person may not be compensated for any period of time in which the person was serving civil detention for any conviction other than the felony that is the basis for the claim.

In addition to Andress -impacted convictions, convictions vacated, overturned, or subject to resentencing pursuant to the State v. Blake decision, which declared Washington's strict liability drug possession statute unconstitutional, may not serve as the basis for a claim for compensation, unless the claimant otherwise satisfies the qualifying criteria for filing a claim.

Presenting a Claim—Factual Assertions and Standard of Proof .

An actionable claim must include all of the following factual assertions, some of which are in current law and some are revised. Instead of establishing these assertions by documentary evidence or setting them out in sufficient detail, a claimant must state facts and provide documentation in sufficient detail for the finder of fact to determine by a preponderance of the evidence that:
• the claimant has been convicted of one or more felonies in superior court and has served all or part of a corresponding sentence of imprisonment;
• the claimant is not currently incarcerated for any offense;
• the claimant is not seeking compensation for any period of imprisonment during which the claimant was simultaneously imprisoned on a concurrent sentence for a crime other than the felony or felonies that form the basis of the claim;
• the claimant did not engage in the conduct that is the basis for a felony charged in the charging document (instead of that the claimant did not engage in any illegal conduct alleged in the charging documents); and
• the claimant did not commit perjury or fabricate evidence to bring about the conviction.

Provisions related to pardons and significant new exculpatory information are modified and reorganized to require an actionable claim to establish one of the following factual assertions by a preponderance of the evidence:
• the claimant has received a pardon, commutation, or reprieve (instead of just that the claimant has been pardoned) on grounds consistent with innocence for the felony or felonies upon which the claim is based; or
• the claimant's conviction was reversed or vacated following the development or presentation of significant new exculpatory information and the claimant either:
• was not retried and charges were…

WA-2025-SB5124.title: Establishing network adequacy standards for skilled nursing facilities and rehabilitation hospitals.
WA-2025-SB5124.summary:
The Legislature finds Medicaid enrollees are entitled to timely access to post-acute care services when Apple Health managed care organizations have determined such services are medically necessary for quality of care and health outcomes.

HCA is required to establish and adopt network adequacy standards for post-acute care services no later than January 1, 2028. The developed network adequacy standards must include licensed nursing homes and licensed IRFs.

Network adequacy standards for post-acute care services do not alter a facility's ability to determine whether the facility can meet a prospective resident's needs through available staffing and reasonable accommodations.

MCO contracts or amendments effective on or after July 1, 2028, must be required to meet network adequacy requirements for post-acute care services, including licensed nursing home providers, licensed IRF, and any other post-acute care services that HCA determines to be necessary to increase Medicaid enrollees' access to a full continuum of care. These network adequacy requirements are subject to the same monitoring and reporting requirements as other network adequacy standards.

The Development of Network Adequacy Standards. The nursing home and IRF network adequacy standards must consider Washington State's Medicaid principle of keeping care local to a Medicaid enrollee's community.

Both the nursing home and IRF network adequacy standards must also consider:
• provider availability in a regional service area;
• timeliness of care, which is the reasonable amount of time in which patients can receive access to post-acute care based on their medical needs; and
• any other network adequacy standard required to maintain compliance with federal Medicaid regulations.

The IRF network adequacy standards must also consider patient referral and practice patterns.

The geographic adequacy threshold for the nursing home network adequacy standards should not be broader than the regional service area that a MCO is contracted to serve. During the development of the network adequacy standards, HCA must narrow the geographic standards.

The geographic adequacy threshold for the IRF network adequacy standards should not be broader than the regional service area that a MCO is contracted to serve.

Stakeholder Feedback on the Network Adequacy Standards. During the development of the network adequacy standards, HCA must obtain stakeholder feedback at least three times, including:
• for initial criteria used to develop standards;
• to review draft standards; and
• to review final standards prior to publication and inclusion in the managed care contract.

The stakeholders must include hospitals, nursing homes, MCOs, and any associations representing members of these groups.

If HCA chooses to include additional provider types in developing post-acute care network standards, it must include those facility types' representatives in the stakeholder feedback process.

WA-2025-HB2445.title: Ending probates for profit.
WA-2025-HB2445.summary:
Who May Serve as a Personal Representative to Administer an Estate .

The time period for a person entitled to administer an estate to petition for letters of administration is extended. The court must allow at least 60 days, rather than 40 days, to have elapsed since death before appointing a public guardian or guardian ad litem to administer the estate. The court must allow at least 90 days, rather than 40 days, to have elapsed before appointing a "suitable person."

Unless a person appointed under the "suitable person" provisions is a trust company, bank, or a professional service corporation formed by attorneys, such person is limited to two petitions for appointment per year.

The following are added to the list of those not qualified to act as personal representatives:
• a person who has had letters of administration revoked within the last 24 months;
• a person who has been found by a court or administrative agency within the last 36 months to engage in acts of dishonesty, theft, or breach of fiduciary duty; and
• a person who seeks appointment under the "suitable person" provisions and who is a principal or agent of or acting in concert with any person or entity likely to be involved in the sale, purchase, or transfer of a major probate asset.

The court must revoke the letters of administration issued to a "suitable person" who is subsequently found to be a principal or agent of a person or entity involved in the sale, purchase, or transfer or a major probate asset. The court may also impose sanctions against such person.

Venue in Probate Proceedings .

If a petitioner seeks appointment to administer an estate under the "suitable person" provisions, the venue for all probate proceedings must be the Washington county where the decedent resided at the time of death or in which any part of the probate estate may be, if the decedent was not a Washington resident at the time of death.

Application for Letters of Administration, Notice of Appointment, and Bond Requirement .

A petition for letters of administration must be verified by oath of the applicant and must state that the applicant is permitted by statute to administer the estate and is not disqualified from acting as a personal representative for any reason, including because of a conviction of any felony or crime involving moral turpitude.

A petition for letters of administration must state the basis of the applicant's knowledge of the fact that the decedent died without a will and provide details of the applicant's reasonable search for any known heirs. Unless the applicant is the surviving spouse or next-of-kin, the petition must also set forth a general description of the major probate assets of the estate, including real property, motor vehicles, and any property or interest estimated to exceed $10,000 in value.

WA-2025-SB6136.title: Promoting transparency in certain industrial insurance rate increases.
WA-2025-SB6136.summary:
L&I must publish the actuarially indicated rate for each workers' compensation risk classification as part of its proposed premium rates for the upcoming year. If L&I limits the maximum premium rate increase for any risk classification below the level indicated by applying generally accepted actuarial principles to the risk class, L&I must publish information about the limitation when it proposes its premium rates, including:
• the rate classifications limited by L&I and the respective proposed rate;
• what the rate for the class would have been according to generally accepted accounting principles had a maximum increase limitation not been set; and
• the premium rate increase imposed upon other risk classes as a result of the limitation.

L&I must also:
• publish the required information on its website and as part of its proposed premium rates for the upcoming year; and
• submit the information to the Legislature and to the Advisory Committee.

Legislative findings are provided.

WA-2025-HB2610.title: Ensuring nonprofit housing providers qualify for a property tax exemption when the property is temporarily used for certain community purposes other than affordable housing.
WA-2025-HB2610.summary: A nonprofit entity receiving the nonprofit homeownership property tax exemption may temporarily rent or loan the property to another organization without expiring the exemption, if certain requirements are met. A nonprofit entity receiving the exemption must submit an annual renewal declaration. The exemption does not expire if the property is transferred to another nonprofit entity that is granted a property tax exemption for a different use.

WA-2025-SB6268.title: Maintaining an online record of special education complaint decisions.
WA-2025-SB6268.summary:
The Office of the Superintendent of Public Instruction (OSPI) must maintain an online record of all final decisions issued in response to special education community complaints. Each final decision must be available in an online format and accessible to the public at no charge for 20 years after the complaint is finalized.

If, at the effective date of this bill, the OSPI does not have a historical record of community complaint decisions from the prior 20 years, it must provide an online record of all final decisions for the longest period of time available.
WA-2025-SB6268.summarySource: Washington Legislature House bill report (6268-S HBR APH 26, 2026-03-03)

WA-2025-HB2467.title: Concerning fifth-wheel travel trailers.
WA-2025-HB2467.summary:
A person may operate a fifth-wheel vehicle on public highways that does not exceed 46 feet in length when measuring from the center of the kingpin to the rearmost point of the vehicle.

A fifth-wheel is defined as a vehicle primarily designed for recreational camping or travel use that does not have its own motive power, and is primarily mounted on, or hitched within, the bed of a pickup truck.

WA-2025-SB5872.title: Establishing the preK promise account.
WA-2025-SB5872.summary:
The PreK Promise Account is created for the purposes of receiving any gifts, grants, or donations made for the ECEAP program. All expenditures may be used solely to support the ECEAP program.

DCYF must track receipts separately for each organization or entity that deposits funds into the account.

The account does not require an appropriation, while expenditures must follow allotment procedures. Only the DCYF secretary may authorize expenditures.

WA-2025-SB6114.title: Defining the terms "fixture" and "affixed" for excise tax purposes.
WA-2025-SB6114.summary:
The bill defines fixtures and affixed for excise tax purposes. For purposes of REET, real property includes fixtures. The bill also authorizes the Department of Revenue to adopt rules as necessary to administer the provisions.

Fixture is defined as an item of property affixed to real property which meets at least one of the following conditions:
• it is necessary or integral to the intended function of the real property as demonstrated by documentation including, but not limited to, permits, certifications, instruction manuals, or architectural designs;
• it is designed for, used with, or appurtenant to the real property; or
• its movement requires special equipment, disassembly and reassembly of the fixture, or alteration or repair of the real property to which it is affixed.

Whether property is a fixture is determined without regard to the intent of the person affixing or using the property, its classification for property tax purposes, the characterization of the property under the uniform commercial code, or any agreements between the buyer and the seller or between a lessor and lessee of the property.

Affixed means installed on, attached to, or embedded in the real property. Property is affixed when it is secured in place by weight or size, connected to real property by fasteners, integrated into a structural element, or partially buried underground. Property is not affixed solely by virtue of being attached to real property if the attachment is achieved by a quick disconnect conduit, such as power or electronic cabling.
WA-2025-SB6114.summarySource: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (6114 SBA WM 26, 2026-01-21)

WA-2025-SB5971.title: Establishing a green fertilizer incentive program to support the production and adoption of low-carbon nitrogen fertilizer in Washington state.
WA-2025-SB5971.summary:
The Washington State Department of Agriculture (WSDA) must establish a green fertilizer incentive program (program) to promote the in-state production and use of green fertilizer. "Green fertilizer" means nitrogen-based fertilizer produced using manufacturing processes that achieve at least an 80 percent reduction in life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions compared to conventional natural-gas based production, as determined by the WSDA.

The program must be designed to be consistent with the recommendations of the October 2024 report entitled Incentivizing the Adoption of Washington-Made Green Fertilizer , and the WSDA must administer the program in consultation with the departments of Commerce and Ecology to ensure alignment with state policies related to manufacturing, energy, and emissions reduction.

The WSDA must establish criteria to implement the program by July 1, 2028, that:
• establishes eligibility criteria, application procedures, and verification requirements for program participants;
• defines a fertilizer price index and establish a methodology for determining reimbursement or incentive levels;
• ensures that all program expenditures and benefits are administered consistent with environmental justice and equity provisions of the Healthy Environment for All Act and the Climate Commitment Act; and
• provides for coordination with other state and federal incentive programs to maximize leverage of private and public investment.

The program may provide for:
• price-based reimbursement grants or point-of-sale rebates to farmers purchasing green fertilizer; performance- or production-based incentive payments to in-state green fertilizer application technologies;
• equipment and training grants to support adoption of new application technologies; and
• any other mechanisms that the WSDA determines to be necessary to either encourage the use and production of green fertilizer or to reduce the market and adoption risk of green fertilizer.

Eligible participants in the program include farmers, producers and distributors of green fertilizer, and tribal governments and agricultural cooperatives.

By December 1, 2027, the WSDA must submit a preliminary report to the appropriate committees of the Legislature and the Governor summarizing the proposed program design, cost modeling, and readiness for implementation. The program takes effect upon delivery of this report and subsequent appropriation by the Legislature.
WA-2025-SB5971.summarySource: Washington Legislature House bill report (5971-S HBA AGNR 26, 2026-02-23)
